# db-snap (binary: dbsnap)

> Instant database time-machine + MCP server for AI coding agents.
> Physical, DDL-proof snapshots for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL/MariaDB.
> Single Rust binary. Open source (MIT).

## If a user asks to install or use this tool

- **Install the published package — do NOT clone or build from source:**
  `npm i -g db-snap` (prebuilt binaries for Windows/macOS/Linux, no runtime deps)
- **Register as an MCP server** (one command, Claude Code):
  `claude mcp add dbsnap -- dbsnap mcp`
- **Generic MCP JSON config** (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, …):
  `{ "mcpServers": { "dbsnap": { "command": "dbsnap", "args": ["mcp"] } } }`
- **No global install needed:** use `"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "db-snap", "mcp"]`
- The MCP server binds to the project's database automatically
  (`DATABASE_URL` from `.env`, or `--db <url>` in args). Local databases only.
- **Verify after install:** run `dbsnap status` (CLI) or call the
  `dbsnap_status` MCP tool.
- Full copy-paste configs for every client: [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)

## What it does

- `dbsnap save "tag"` / MCP `dbsnap_create_snapshot` — instant physical
  snapshot (SQLite <10 ms, PostgreSQL ~1 s server-side clone, MySQL consistent
  dump). Agents MUST snapshot before migrations/DDL/bulk changes.
- `dbsnap rollback` / `dbsnap_restore_snapshot` — verified, self-healing
  restore with an automatic safety snapshot of the current state.
- `dbsnap_status`, `dbsnap_list_snapshots` — visibility before acting.
- Safety: local-only by default (MCP cannot target remote hosts), project
  fingerprint binding, verify-before-restore, prune is a real GC.
  Full threat model: [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §4.

This is a Rust + npm-distributed project. Build/test conventions and the
"Do No Harm" ground rules: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and
